title: <form action> & useFormStatus: Form Lifecycle and Pending State

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In standard HTML, submitting a form sends data and refreshes the whole page. In React 19, you can hand a JavaScript function straight to `<form action={myAction}>`. When you click submit, React gathers all the inputs into a `FormData` bundle, sends it, and lets any button inside the form know that it is currently 'loading' without passing props down.
progressiveExplaining.junior: React 19 extends standard HTML forms by accepting async functions in `<form action={fn}>`, `<button formAction={fn}>`, and `<input formAction={fn}>`. React automatically extracts and passes the native `FormData` object to the action function. The `useFormStatus` hook lets child components read the parent form's submission state (`pending`, `data`, `method`, `action`) without prop drilling.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, React DOM actions unify client-side JavaScript transitions with progressive enhancement. When JavaScript is enabled, React intercepts form submission, prevents full-page reload, wraps the action execution in a transition lane, and sets `pending = true` in `useFormStatus`. If JavaScript fails to load or is disabled (in frameworks supporting SSR/Server Actions like Next.js), the form falls back to standard HTTP POST submission.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: React overrides the native HTML form submit event handler. When `<form action={asyncFn}>` fires, React instantiates `new FormData(formElement)`, invokes the action within a transition context (`startHostTransition`), and sets an internal `HostTransitionContext` on the fiber tree. `useFormStatus` reads this context from parent fibers to expose the pending state and submitted `FormData` directly.

rosettaStone.react: `<form action={asyncAction}>` with `useFormStatus()` in child submit buttons.

codeComparison.title: Manual e.preventDefault() + Local Loading State vs Native React 19 Form Action
codeComparison.summary: Manual submit handlers require boilerplate state and prop drilling; React 19 handles FormData extraction and status tracking natively.

interviewGotchas.question: Where can `useFormStatus` be called in the component tree?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your understanding of Context boundaries in React DOM.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `useFormStatus` **must be called from a component rendered inside the `<form>`**, not in the component that renders the `<form>` itself. It behaves like a React Context consumer: calling it in the parent component rendering the `<form>` will return `pending: false` because it cannot read its own child form's status context.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Placing `const { pending } = useFormStatus()` in the same component that returns `<form>...</form>` will not work; extract the submit button into a separate child component.

interviewGotchas.question: What happens if an action function returns a value or throws an error?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of error propagation during form action dispatch.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: If a `<form action>` function throws an error, React catches the exception and propagates it to the nearest **Error Boundary**. If you want to capture form return values or validation errors as local component state without throwing, use `useActionState` instead of a plain `<form action>`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not expect `<form action={fn}>` to set a return value onto form state automatically; pair it with `useActionState` when response data is needed.
